text:
alex: quick sync — sketching an "edge-normalization" shim to unify hosted/dedicated/private runtimes. goal: single runtime adapter, small translation layer for auth/telemetry/capabilities. throwing ideas out.

maria: is this a sidecar proxy or a library? what are hard requirements?

alex: primarily a tiny sidecar (proxy) with a library fallback for air-gapped installs. responsibilities: map local auth to canonical claims, normalize telemetry envelopes, emit capability headers, and expose a pluggable redaction hook. no request routing logic, no heavy state. keep runtime unchanged.

jonathan: perf note — any proxy in hot path can hurt p99. we should define an explicit bypass path for ultra-low-latency routes and an in-process shim alternative.

sara: private installs also have KMS/HSM constraints. shim must accept a credentials-provider interface so it can sign/assert tokens locally instead of calling our hosted KMS.

paul: auth variants: hosted uses ephemeral bearer tokens, dedicated may use internal IAM, private often wants mTLS + signed tokens. how does runtime stay auth-agnostic?

alex: define canonical claims surface: tenant_id, role, request_id, call_chain. shim adapters map local auth -> these claims. runtime reads only those claims via header or local socket handshake.

maria: good. versioning risk — older private shims may not understand new claims. add a version header and capability flags.

jonathan: capability flags are important for KV-cache semantics. example cap: kv-prefix-stable=true/false. runtime can decide to enable cross-request cache reuse only if stable.

alex: proposed headers: X-RW-Edge-Version: 1.0.0; X-RW-Edge-Caps: kv-prefix-stable=1,telemetry-v2=0

paul: telemetry: some enterprise customers will block raw spans or require redaction. shim must allow plugin redactors or a local sidecar that filters PII before egress. default: no-op. config should permit sink selection (internal collector vs local SIEM).

sara: define redactor API minimal: redact(json_record) -> json_record | null. allow wasm or native plugin. document expectations for latency cost.

jonathan: tests: need deterministic batch id derivation tests. if shard/batching depends on keys derived from request metadata, shim must preserve that derivation exactly across all hosting modes. we should include an interop test harness.

alex: agreed. plan: small integration suite that runs (hosted-shim + runtime) vs (lib-shim + runtime) vs (private-shim + runtime) on identical synthetic traces and asserts tokenization, batch IDs, and p99 within thresholds.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created job edge-normalization-integration-nightly (schedule: nightly).

maria: failure modes? if shim crashes, should we fail open or closed? what's the safe default?

paul: security posture: default fail-closed for production/paid routes. dev mode may allow fail-open with explicit flag. config keys: fail_mode=[closed|open], allow_direct_bypass=[true|false], version_policy=[strict|backcompat].

alex: rollout idea: 1) RFC + docs and version scheme, 2) in-proc shim integration tests, 3) hosted canary behind ff, 4) invite 1-2 private customers for pilot with library shim or sidecar as they prefer.

sara: for private customers who can't run a network proxy, provide a tiny library that exposes the same mapping API — avoids network hop and respects local KMS. call this "lib-edge".

maria: can someone draft a config example? quick YAML to show defaults.

alex: short example:

```
edge_normalizer:
  version: "1.0.0"
  fail_mode: closed
  allow_direct_bypass: false
  caps:
    kv-prefix-stable: true
    telemetry-v2: false
  auth_adapter: mtls_adapter
  telemetry:
    redactor: ./plugins/local_redactor.wasm
    sink: internal-collector
```

paul: i can take auth adapters (mtls + ephemeral token mapping). alex you own overall design + interop tests?

alex: i'll own design + tests. @maria please draft a short RFC with diagrams and versioning charter.

maria: will do today and circulate.

jonathan: i'll build the perf harness and run throughput/latency numbers. aim to share initial numbers in 4 days.

sara: i'll enumerate private install KMS/HSM constraints and redaction/legal notes.

alex: next steps: RFC -> spike -> canary. add ARCH ticket and link nightly CI. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
